text:
aria: Heads-up — seeing a 95th-percentile host-side latency jump on streaming requests after yesterday's runtime push. Spike sits in parse/tokenize when concurrency >120.

mike: saw it on dashboards, /ingress/preparse CPU stays hot. any traces? :thinking_face:

aria: attaching pprof excerpt: 
```
(pprof) top
3.2s 30.5% runtime.parseToken
1.8s 17.1% net.http2.parseFrame
0.9s 8.6% kvcache.lookup
0.7s 6.6% grpc.streamSlice
0.5s 4.7% runtime.alloc
```

aria: KV cache miss rate also ~2x for these streaming windows, which drives more fallback parse work.

jamie: any kernel-selection or batching heuristic changes land recently? could be that conservative kernels increased parse cost.

sasha: I merged a batching heuristic tweak last week (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1789) that biases larger batches for low-latency tiers. Might affect bufferization and parse interleaving.

olivia: I'll repro with harness that drives streaming lots of small chunks. can run repeatable.

mike: use this command against canary:
```
./tools/harness --mode streaming --concurrency 150 --chunk-ms 12 --duration 120 --target canary-host:8080
```

aria: ran 2m, repro stable. diffing preparse traces shows lots of small write syscalls (smallwrite pattern) causing http2/hpack stalls -> parseFrame cost up.

jamie: smallwrite pattern suggests writev coalescing got lost. a shim revert in 2024-02 build may be related.

sasha: right — we reverted the write coalesce to fix an ordering flake. I can reintroduce writev coalesce behind a flag.

mike: before IO surgery, can we mitigate at tokenize? aria, current tokenize alloc behavior? maybe a streaming lexer avoids per-fragment allocs.

aria: microbench: current tokenizer ~0.5 allocs/op for fragments <64B. streaming lexer drops to ~0.05 allocs/op.

olivia: patch idea: fast-path in preparse: if payload <128B and headers stable, use in-place streaming lexer + zero-copy ref. low-risk.

sre-bot: Incident IN-2024-042 created (host-preparse-latency). Assigned eng-runtime.

mike: also add KV instrumentation to understand miss causes — maybe eviction thrash as batches include more distinct prefixes.

aria: added kv tags on canary, sample: 
```
kv.metrics: requests=23k hits=18k misses=5k miss_rate=0.217 eviction_rate=0.03
hot_shard=13 hit_rate=0.60
```

aria: miss spikes line up with concurrency peaks.

jamie: points to batching causing poorer key locality. sasha's change likely root cause.

sasha: I'll add a streaming-aware tweak: cap micro-batch size to 8 for streaming to keep per-connection locality. Will land as flag.

mike: test matrix on canary: (1) re-enable coalesce, (2) streaming-lexer fast-path, (3) batch-cap for streams. each alone then combined.

olivia: running harness + pprof + kv metrics. timeline:
- 1749803000 baseline canary run
- 1749803600 canary + lexer
- 1749804200 canary + batchcap
- 1749804567 combined

aria: quick results:
- baseline: 95p=210ms, parseToken=30%
- +lexer: 95p=160ms, parseToken=18%, allocs/op down
- +batchcap: 95p=175ms, kv_miss_rate -> 0.12
- combined: 95p=120ms, kv_miss_rate=0.09, parseToken=12%

jamie: throughput slightly down (~3% qps) on combined but tail improvements look worth it.

mike: open PR to wire as feature flags for streaming routes, include perf tests. https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1833

sasha: prepping canary rollout. deploy-bot, start canary when PR merged.

deploy-bot: Started canary deploy runtime-canary id=canary-20240210 targeting eng-runtime (3 nodes)

olivia: monitoring. if stable for 2 hours, promote and schedule for next patch cut.

aria: follow-ups: 1% kv trace sampling, add unit/integration tests for lexer fast-path.

mike: good triage. add to postmortem notes if recurrence. :thumbsup:
